info.title: Queek API Docs
info.description:
Build a store's website on its Queek catalogue: products, collections, promotions, reviews, pages and blog, plus a cart that hands off to Queek checkout. Read llms.txt on this host for the guide.

## Errors

Every error answers `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "errors"?, "doc_url", "request_id"}}`, alongside the
legacy top-level keys. Switch on `error.code`, never on the message. Codes: `ai_unavailable_in_test_mode`, `api_key_expired`, `api_key_mode_mismatch`, `api_key_revoked`, `app_embed_not_ready`, `app_grant_insufficient`, `app_handoff_failed`, `app_installation_gone`, `app_installation_pending`, `app_ip_not_allowed`, `app_proxy_failed`, `app_proxy_gone`, `app_token_revoked`, `bad_request`, `client_key_required`, `conflict`, `custom_gateway_forbidden`, `custom_gateway_kyc_required`, `custom_gateway_not_configured`, `custom_gateway_not_verified`, `custom_gateway_plan_required`, `custom_gateway_store_ineligible`, `custom_gateway_verification_failed`, `forbidden`, `gone`, `idempotency_key_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reuse`, `insufficient_scope`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_client_key`, `metafield_definition_missing`, `metafield_filter_unsupported_type`, `metafield_namespace_reserved`, `metafield_value_invalid`, `metaobject_definition_missing`, `metaobject_field_invalid`, `metaobject_reference_invalid`, `metaobject_type_reserved`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `origin_not_allowed`, `origin_required`, `payload_too_large`, `payment_amount_mismatch`, `plan_inactive`, `private_key_required`, `requires_slot`, `resync_cooldown`, `route_not_available`, `server_error`, `service_unavailable`, `subscription_feature_locked`, `too_many_requests`, `unauthenticated`, `unknown_product_ref`, `unknown_service`, `unknown_variant_ref`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_failed`, `vendor_access_denied`, `vendor_mail_sender_forbidden`, `vendor_mail_sender_not_configured`, `vendor_mail_sender_plan_required`, `vendor_mail_sender_verification_failed`.
Each error carries `doc_url` pointing at its own entry in the error reference.

## Request ids

Send `X-Request-Id` (8–128 chars matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) to correlate your trace with ours,
or read the one we generate — it is echoed on every response, error bodies included, and appears on every log line
of the request. `X-Queek-Api-Version` carries the API version (`v1`).

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` on a write and a retry cannot execute twice. Same key + same body replays the stored
response verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24h. Same key + a different body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A concurrent duplicate waits 15s for the first to finish, then replays;
past that it is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Responses ≥ 400 are not stored, so a failure stays retryable.
The slot is vendor + caller + METHOD:path + key. The body is the fingerprint, not part of the slot. Operations that accept the header document it as a parameter.

## Rate limits

180 requests/min per API key + IP, or storefront origin + IP when no key is sent. On top of that, a private (`sk_live_`) key carries its
store's plan quota: `free` 60/min, `social_media` 120/min, `starter` 120/min, `growth` 240/min, `scale` 1200/min, `enterprise` 2400/min. sk_live_ private keys only. A pk_live_ public key is shared by every visitor of the store, so it gets no per-store bucket.
Exceeding either is `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an endpoint per store and Queek posts the signed event to it. Topics are listed under `webhooks`
in this document; the body is signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>` —
over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, tolerance 300s. A rotation keeps the previous secret valid for
24h and sends both signatures, space delimited. Delivery is 8 attempts on a published backoff;
an endpoint failing for 24h is disabled and the merchant notified.

channel.description:
`channel` is the inbox (messaging) channel, typed against
MessagingChannel — never the sales channel. An importing app
recognises its own orders one key further down.

custom_channel.description:
Import recognition: the sales channel that imported the order
(chowdeck, glovo — null for every other order) and the outside
platform's own reference (null unless imported). Together with
`platform` (third_party) an app matches orders events to its
own records with no link table. Additive: both keys are null
for every order that is not an import.

currency.description:
Vendor chain with the same unloaded-relation safety net as the
sibling order shapes: loaded relation first, then the
cache-backed lookup — never the silent platform default.

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties (jsonb, array-cast). Absent lines
render an empty object, never null — apps always see the key.
An app's single-use keys (claims, manage links) reach only the
app that issued them, never another app or key.

metafields.description:
The receiver's own fields coming back to them: typed metafields the
merchant defined, and the opaque metadata an integrator wrote. This
is the whole point of order extensions — a webhook that omits the
ERP id forces the receiver to make a second call to match the order
to their own record.

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties. Always present as an object so
dashboard chips and the shopper page never branch on absence.
Bearer keys are withheld here too (dashboard, shopper page,
rider): the order email is their only carrier.

original.description:
Full original for hero-scale surfaces (featured/promo blocks render
~1100-1320 physical px — the 480px card upscales blurry there).

image_variants.description:
Additive — see decision_tree.json image-variants-contract-pr1/2.
null when the primary image isn't Media-backed (raw URL only) or
'variants' wasn't eager-loaded; existing keys above are unaffected.

metafields.description:
Vendor-defined typed fields, keyed `namespace.key`. `{}` for a store
that has defined none, which costs no query (MetafieldPresenter).
Free-form `metadata` is deliberately NOT here: it is an
integrator's private bookkeeping and stays on the merchant API.
Client surface: draft entries and storefront-hidden definitions
are omitted from reference values (MetafieldPresenter).

0.description:
The handoff for a vendor-built frontend: send the buyer here and the
hosted storefront adopts this exact cart (?cart= wins on any URL) and
runs checkout, payment and delivery on Queek. Guest carts only —
that is the token the storefront can adopt.

rider_approved.description:
Whether this rider may actually open the storefront rider console —
is_rider alone is not enough, a vendor approval path must have
stamped rider_approved_at (see EnsureClientRider). The storefront
shows a "pending approval" state when is_rider && ! rider_approved.

image_variants.description:
Pre-sized copies of the image, resolved from its URL (categories
and collections store no media id).

the reset code. Declared here (rather than inline on the route) so the
public reference shows the body.

code.description: Stable identifier a client switches on. A new failure mode gets a new code; an existing code never changes meaning.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable — never switch on it.

field.description: First offending field, on validation failures only.

errors.description: Per-field validation messages, on validation failures only.

doc_url.description: Deep link to this code in the error reference: https://docs.usequeek.com/docs/versioning-and-errors#<code>.

request_id.description: The X-Request-Id of this request. Quote it in support.

QueekMetafieldType.description:
A metafield definition's `type`. Scalar forms, plus `list.<type>` for each listable one.

Limits (shared Postgres, part of the contract): 200 definitions per store, 50 values per resource, 65536 bytes per serialized value. Free-form `metadata`: 50 keys, key ≤ 64 chars, value ≤ 500 chars.

Reserved namespaces (a store may not define in these): `queek`.
Owner types wired in this version: `product`, `order`.

partial.description:
Opt-in only — omit it (or send false) for a full cart save; send
true only when syncing some of the items and leaving the rest
of the saved cart untouched.

content.description:
Self-heal on serve: run stored blocks through the canonical
normalizer so a legacy/malformed section (e.g. a gallery with a
null slide) can never crash the storefront render. Same sanitizer
the write path uses, so serving == what a re-save would produce.
Pre-normalized above (attachContentMediaVariants also collects
media_index from this exact array) rather than re-normalized here,
so content[] and media_index can never disagree with each other.

stores. One flag per fact: dev_store says WHAT it is,
password_required gates the token; this response itself

storefront to noindex + drop it from sitemap/feed/agents.

QueekStoreAuthSession.description: The customer session. Send `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; rotate with `POST auth/token/refresh` before `expires_at`.

is_new_user.description: Always true here — this endpoint creates the account.
